# Export Compliance Procedure

**[Company Name] | Version 1.0 | Owner: Export Compliance Officer (ECO) | Effective: [date] | Reviewed annually**

## 1. Purpose and scope
As a US company, we are subject to US export controls (the EAR, administered by Commerce/BIS) and US sanctions (administered by Treasury/OFAC) wherever our customers are. This covers SaaS access, downloadable apps, SDKs/APIs, source code, and technical information shared with non-US persons. It applies to all employees, contractors, and resellers.

## 2. Roles
- **ECO** ([e.g., COO or GC]): owns this procedure, decides escalations, keeps records, engages outside counsel.
- **Sales/RevOps:** screens customers and partners before contract or activation.
- **Finance:** screens vendors and payees; flags payments tied to restricted locations.
- **Engineering:** maintains product classifications and geo-blocking.
- **People Ops:** flags non-US hires and contractors for access review.

## 3. Product classification
- Classify each product and major version. Because of encryption, most SaaS products are **5D992.c (mass market)** or **5D002 eligible for License Exception ENC**. Record the ECCN and the reasoning.
- Confirm whether any BIS encryption reporting (e.g., the annual self-classification report due Feb 1) applies to us.
- Re-classify when adding new cryptography, on-prem/downloadable versions, or specialized technical capabilities.

## 4. Restricted destinations (blocked by default)
- **Cuba, Iran, North Korea**, and the **Crimea, so-called DNR and LNR regions** of Ukraine.
- **Russia and Belarus**: extensive EAR restrictions, plus OFAC bans on certain IT and cloud-software services.
- **Heightened review:** Syria (rules changed substantially in 2025), Venezuela, and anything else the ECO adds. The ECO checks this list monthly.

**Controls:** IP geo-blocking at signup and login; block billing addresses, cards, and phone numbers from these locations; restrict app-store availability; monitor for VPN/proxy use from blocked regions.

## 5. Restricted-party screening
- Screen every customer (automated for self-serve; before signature for enterprise), reseller, vendor, and payee against the **Consolidated Screening List** (includes the OFAC SDN, BIS Entity, Denied Persons, Unverified, and Military End-User lists).
- Apply OFAC's **50% rule**: entities owned 50% or more, in aggregate, by blocked persons are blocked even if unlisted. Collect ownership information from enterprise customers.
- Re-screen the entire customer base automatically when lists update (at least weekly).
- **Potential match:** hold provisioning, escalate to the ECO within one business day, and don't tell the customer why until the ECO approves.

## 6. Red flags: stop and escalate
- Evasive answers about end user, end use, or ownership.
- Location, IP, and payment details that don't match.
- Uses connected to military, nuclear, missile, chemical/biological weapons, or surveillance activities.
- Military or government end users in China, Russia, or other countries of concern.
- Resellers with no identified end customer; unusual payment routing or third-party payers.

Never ignore red flags or avoid asking questions. "We didn't ask" is not a defense.

## 7. Internal access and deemed exports
Sharing controlled technology or source code with foreign nationals, even inside the US, can be an export. People Ops flags non-US hires and contractors, and the ECO confirms their access is permitted (it usually is for EAR99 or ENC-eligible technology). No employee or contractor may access our systems or code from a restricted destination. Check with the ECO before taking company laptops to a restricted destination.

## 8. Contracts
Terms of Service, order forms, and reseller agreements must include:
- an export/sanctions compliance clause;
- customer representations that it is not a restricted party, is not owned by one, and is not located in a restricted region;
- our right to suspend or terminate immediately.

Reseller agreements must also require resellers to screen their own customers.

## 9. Escalation and suspected violations
Report any suspected violation to the ECO immediately. The ECO brings in outside counsel. Preserve all records and do not delete accounts or data. The ECO and counsel decide on suspension, blocking or rejecting funds, required OFAC reports (blocked property must be reported within 10 business days), and voluntary self-disclosure to OFAC or BIS. There is no retaliation for good-faith reporting.

## 10. Training, records, and review
- **Training:** at onboarding and annually for Sales, Finance, Support, Engineering leads, and People Ops.
- **Records:** keep classifications, screening results, escalations, and transaction records for **10 years**. That is OFAC's requirement; the EAR requires 5.
- **Review:** the ECO runs an annual self-audit and reports the results to the CEO.

**Approved:** ____________ (CEO) ____________ (ECO) Date: ________

*This template is a starting point. Have export-control counsel review it before you adopt it.*

**PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL: ATTORNEY-CLIENT COMMUNICATION, PREPARED AT THE DIRECTION OF COUNSEL**

# MEMORANDUM

**To:** CEO; [limited leadership distribution]
**From:** [General Counsel / Head of Compliance]
**Date:** [date]
**Re:** Customer 55% owned by an SDN: immediate actions and next steps

## 1. Bottom line
We have learned that [Customer] is 55% owned by [Parent], which is on OFAC's Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List. Under OFAC's 50 Percent Rule, an entity owned 50% or more by blocked persons (directly or indirectly, individually or in aggregate) is itself blocked, even if it is not named on the list. US persons, including us, generally may not provide services to it, accept payments from it, or otherwise deal in its property. Our roughly eight months of service may therefore be apparent violations.

This is serious but manageable. OFAC gives significant weight to stopping promptly, cooperating, fixing the problem, and disclosing it voluntarily. Keep this matter within the working group named below.

## 2. Immediate actions (next 24–72 hours)
1. **Stop service now.** Suspend the account, support, and any professional services. No renewals, upgrades, or new invoices. **Do not delete** the account or its data.
2. **Retain outside sanctions counsel today** so the investigation is privileged.
3. **Make no refunds, credits, data exports, or other transfers** to the customer. Each of these is itself a prohibited dealing with a blocked person.
4. **Block property we hold.** Funds we hold or receive for the customer, such as incoming payments or credit balances, generally must go into a blocked, interest-bearing account and be reported to OFAC within 10 business days. Counsel will advise on three open questions: amounts already received, unpaid receivables (collecting them requires an OFAC license), and whether hosted customer data must be held as blocked property.
5. **Alert Finance.** Turn off auto-billing. Any contact with our bank or payment processor goes through counsel, because they may have their own reporting obligations.
6. **Customer notice.** Send only a short, counsel-approved message saying the service is suspended for legal compliance reasons. Offer no negotiation, workaround, or transition help without OFAC authorization.
7. **Legal hold.** Preserve all contracts, onboarding and screening records, invoices, payments, support tickets, emails, and Slack messages about this customer.

## 3. Facts to establish (next 1–2 weeks)
Counsel will lead an investigation into the following:
- **Timing:** When was [Parent] designated, and when did its stake reach 50%? If either happened after our service began, the earlier activity may not be a violation. OFAC may also have issued a general license that authorizes wind-down activity. Check this first.
- **Ownership:** Confirm the 55% figure and find out whether any other blocked persons hold stakes.
- **Program:** Identify which sanctions program applies (e.g., Russia, Iran, counterterrorism). Also check whether the parent is on BIS lists that affect our software.
- **Scope:** Establish dates, products, users and their locations, every payment received, and any software or technical data provided.
- **Knowledge:** Did our screening run? Did anyone see red flags or ownership information? Did the customer misrepresent its ownership? Knowledge and willfulness largely decide whether OFAC treats a case as egregious.
- **Related exposure:** Find any other customers, users, or resellers connected to [Parent]. Check whether EU, UK, or other sanctions reach us through non-US operations.

## 4. Disclosure decision
We should strongly consider a **voluntary self-disclosure (VSD) to OFAC**:
- Under OFAC's Enforcement Guidelines, a VSD cuts the base penalty in half. Many non-egregious cases close with a cautionary letter and no penalty.
- Maximum civil penalties under IEEPA are the greater of more than $375,000 per violation (adjusted annually for inflation) or twice the transaction value. Each payment or service period may count as a separate violation. Willful violations can be prosecuted as crimes.
- The statute of limitations is now 10 years. We lose disclosure credit if OFAC hears about this from someone else first, for example through a bank's blocking report.
- The usual approach is a prompt initial notification, followed by a full report once the investigation is complete.

Counsel will also assess whether we should make a disclosure to BIS.

## 5. Remediation
- Add ownership-based (50% rule) screening for business customers on top of name screening.
- Re-screen the full customer base now, then automatically whenever the lists update.
- Document the root cause and the fixes. OFAC gives heavy weight to improvements in a compliance program.
- Add sanctions representations and immediate-termination rights to our contracts.
- Train Sales, Finance, and Customer Success on ownership red flags and escalation.

## 6. Governance and communications
- **Owner:** [GC]. **Working group:** CEO, CFO, Head of Customer Success, Head of Engineering, and outside counsel.
- Brief the board or audit committee promptly. Counsel will decide whether we owe notice to investors, lenders, insurers, or auditors.
- Send all communication about this matter through counsel. Do not speculate about it or analyze it in email or Slack.
- Please acknowledge receipt and confirm the service suspension by [date/time].
